svg.text: v5 — Per-caller rate limits
PROBLEM: one caller in a loop could spend the server's CPU — 682 ms of bcrypt per anonymous login attempt, unlimited, and a public /classify.
FIX: a token bucket per caller, checked BEFORE the expensive work. An empty bucket is a 429 costing ~6 ms instead of a login costing ~890 ms.
core/rate_limit.py — the token bucket
Each caller has a bucket of at most N tokens.
Each request takes 1 token. Tokens drip back at N per minute.
Empty → 429 + Retry-After: seconds until the next token.
A quiet caller may burst N at once (a person clicking around);
a caller in a loop is held to the refill rate (a script).
PATH A — NO IDENTITY YET: KEY = CLIENT ADDRESS
POST /auth/login {"email": "maya@acme.example", "password": "…"}
Also POST /auth/register — both run bcrypt, both spend the same "auth" budget.
auth/router.py → auth/dependencies.py: limit_auth_attempts()
enforce(request, "auth", key=request.client.host) # 10 / min
Declared on the router, so every /auth endpoint — including future ones — is covered.
token taken
bucket empty
auth/service.py → bcrypt (~890 ms)
Only reached when a token was available.
429 Too Many Requests (~6 ms)
Retry-After: 2
{"detail": "Too many requests"}
Refused BEFORE bcrypt: a test proves authenticate()
is never called for a refused attempt.
PATH B — MODEL INFERENCE: KEY = USER ID
POST /classify or POST /tickets {"text": "I was charged twice"}
Authorization: Bearer eyJ… (/classify was PUBLIC until v5)
auth/dependencies.py: get_current_user() — unchanged from v4
No token → 401 first. An anonymous caller has no budget to spend and learns nothing, not even if the model is loaded.
User(id=7)
auth/dependencies.py: limit_inference()
enforce(request, "inference", key="user:7") # 60 / min
ONE budget for /classify and POST /tickets: both spend the classifier's CPU, so neither can be a side door.
bucket empty
classifier.predict() → 200 / 201
GET /tickets reads spend no inference budget.
429 (~15 ms — not free)
A per-user key needs the user, so the token check and
the users lookup still run before refusal. Per-address
refusal (Path A) needs no database and costs ~6 ms.
Why per user: colleagues behind one office NAT don't share.
Where the buckets live
app.state.rate_limiters, built in main.py create_app().
A dict in ONE process's memory: ~2 µs per check,
~140 bytes per caller, capped at 100,000 callers.
Two uvicorn workers = two dicts = the limit is doubled.
Measured below. Shared state (Redis) is the fix when needed.
MEASURED LOCALLY — ONE SESSION, ONE CLIENT ADDRESS, DB_ECHO=false, NO --reload, httpx CLIENT
limits off: 30 × 401 29.06 s
11 not 10: ~1.5 tokens refilled during
the ~9 s the first ten spent in bcrypt.
limits off: 100 × 200, P50 24.8 ms
57 = 60 − 5 warm-up + ~2 refilled.
Limiter itself: 2.07 µs per check.
limit 5/min, 40 parallel wrong logins
--workers 1: 5 allowed, 35 × 429
--workers 2: 8 allowed, 32 × 429
Up to 10 possible; depends on how the OS
spreads connections across the two workers.
1. Per-process buckets: N workers or N replicas multiply every limit by N — the trigger for a shared store (Redis) the moment we scale out.
2. Per-address limits do not stop a distributed attack: 1,000 addresses × 10 logins/min is still 10,000 bcrypt calls a minute. 3. Reads (GET /tickets) are unlimited.
4. Test suite 103 s → 165 s: /classify tests now need a registered user. 5. Still no token revocation, no type checker. Documents (the knowledge base) not started.
